events.label: Vance speaks at University of Mississippi Turning Point event on immigration obligations
U.S. suspends Microsoft and Adobe from green-card labor program

slots.name: suspension status
slots.sentence: Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that the administration is suspending several tech firms, including Microsoft, from a program that allows H-1B visa holders to apply for green cards.

slots.name: H-1B applications
slots.sentence: She said most of its employees in the U.S. are American citizens and that of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications it submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% were for existing Microsoft employees.

slots.name: H-1B maximum duration
slots.sentence: Companies can employ someone on an H-1B for a maximum of six years and then must then sponsor them for a green card to keep them.

slots.name: replacement ratio
slots.sentence: “For every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker with one-and-a-half foreign indentured servants,” he said, arguing that the company is indicative of a “scandalous system that we’ve allowed in this country for far too long.”
